 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri P.S. Chouhan - Advocate for applicant.
Shri Rajiv Pandey - Panel Lawyer for State.

Order 
Notice has been served to the victim.

Applicant is in detention since 25.04.2025.
2.
As per the prosecution story, allegation against the applicant is of abducting and committing rape with the minor prosecutrix.
On the basis of which, the case was registered against the present applicant under the aforesaid Sections.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the present case.
He is in custody since 25.04.2025.
It is submitted that statement of prosecutrix has been recorded in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:37320 2 MCRC-24375-2025 which she has not supported the prosecution story.
DNA report is also negative.
There is no criminal antecedents of the applicant.
The conclusion of the trial will take considerable time, therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the bail application and prayed for it's rejection.

sentences.text: 5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merit of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Consequently, bail application under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of Cr.P.C.
7 .
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
